# Review user access and privileged accounts

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

On a recurring security cadence and after significant team or system changes. A reviewed access register with unnecessary privileges removed and exceptions owned.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Collect current identities and entitlements

agent-runnable


Export authorized account, role, service-account and privileged-access information from the relevant systems. Reconcile it with current workers, vendors and system owners without including raw credentials.

- Sources: [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Validate business need with accountable owners

human · human approval required


Each system or data owner checks whether access is still needed at its current level. Identify departed users, shared accounts, dormant access and temporary privileges that have no approved expiry.

- Sources: [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Approve removals and controlled exceptions

human · human approval required


The designated approvers review proposed changes, operational dependencies and emergency access. Assign owners and expiry dates to exceptions rather than allowing a reviewer to approve their own unnecessary privilege.

- Sources: [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Apply and verify the authorized changes

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


Administrators remove or adjust approved access and rotate exposed credentials through the established process. Test critical service accounts and preserve company-controlled recovery paths.

- Sources: [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Reconcile evidence and the next review

agent-runnable


Compare the approved decisions with actual entitlements and log unresolved changes. Retain the review evidence, assign remediation owners and schedule the next review.

- Verify: A reviewed access register with unnecessary privileges removed and exceptions owned.
- Sources: [FTC cybersecurity for small business](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/small-businesses/cybersecurity)
